note: Which (reference generator x observer) pairings the library supports, and what stands behind each verdict.
A pairing is a template combination, so nothing in the type system can reject it: `Motor` will happily
compile MTPA against an observer whose model has no d-axis term, and the result is a plausible angle that
is wrong. This file is the register that turns 'we thought about it' into 'someone had to write a verdict'.
allow        -- supported, and the evidence exists.
conditional  -- supported only while a stated condition holds; `condition` must be a sentence a caller
can check against their own machine, and `enforced_by` must say what enforces it.
forbid       -- not supported; `falsifier` must name a case that exists, because 'do not do this' is a
claim like any other and needs something that can go red.
unmeasured   -- nobody has measured it. This is a verdict, not a gap: it says the library makes no claim,
and `reason` must say what would have to be measured to change it.
`pairs` is checked against the headers: every reference generator crossed with every observer must appear.

pairs.why: d is pinned to zero by construction, so the d-axis currents that make the observers disagree with their own flux model never appear.

pairs.condition: i_d_per_speed_a_s_per_rad must be zero or a measured safe rate. At the default rate of zero this pairing is indistinguishable from `NullReferenceGenerator`; any non-zero rate is a claim about how much d-axis current the observer in the slot can carry at that speed.
pairs.enforced_by: MtpaReference::i_d_limit_a() -- the allowance is `rate * abs(omega_e)`, so the rate is the only thing standing between MTPA and an observer that cannot see d-axis current at all.

pairs.condition: abs(i_d) <= rate * abs(omega_e) with the rate taken from the measured table: at i_d = 0 the 0.15 rad ceiling holds from 100 rad/s up, at i_d = -1 A the same observer reads three times the ceiling at 200 rad/s and is harmless at 3200 rad/s. The safe rate is therefore not a constant.
pairs.enforced_by: MtpaReference::i_d_limit_a() with a rate the caller set from test_daxis_observer_limit.cpp; the library defaults the rate to zero rather than guessing one.

pairs.why: The slot's model is a single inductance with a constant flux target, so a non-zero i_d moves the flux it believes it is tracking by `Ld*i_d` with nothing to outvote it at any speed. On the nominal machine that is 0.042 rad at i_d = -1 A, which is *inside* the 0.15 rad ceiling -- so the obvious argument says it is harmless and the argument has never been checked. Measuring it needs a rig that holds a non-zero i_d and reads the observer's angle, which does not exist yet.
pairs.reason: Build the rig, then fill this cell with a measured table like the NLFO one.

pairs.why: The ideal observer is the sensor the observer slot is measured against; it carries no model of the machine and therefore has no parameters to disagree with a non-zero d-axis current.

pairs.condition: The carrier's own estimate is only valid while the saliency signal is above min_hf_current_a, and it is resolved by MagnetPolarityTest before the loop closes. A reference generator that asks for a large negative i_d saturates the saliency it depends on.
pairs.enforced_by: HfiObserver::locked() plus config.min_hf_current_a; the polarity half is a separate, explicitly sequenced step.

pairs.condition: Both of its observers must themselves be allowed with the reference in the slot: the blend interpolates between them, so a pairing that is forbidden on either side is forbidden here (at the weight where that side is in charge).
pairs.enforced_by: Nothing mechanical -- this cell is a rule about how to read the matrix, and it is why the blend's own observers appear in their own rows.
